name: Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope (GMRT)
description: An array of thirty steerable 45 m dishes observing at metre wavelengths (50 to 1,500 MHz), run by the National Centre for Radio Astrophysics of the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research.
highlights: Built under Govind Swarup between 1984 and 1996, it is described as the largest and most sensitive radio telescope array at low frequencies.
In August 2018 it detected TGSS J1530+1049, the most distant known radio galaxy at the time of that report.
In February 2020 it contributed to observations of the Ophiuchus Supercluster explosion.
